title: List with One Bulleted Item

illustrates.quote: To indicate that only some items in the list have bullets or other print indicators, such as pictures: a. Follow print for the symbol used as a bullet. The bullet begins in cell 1 and is followed by a space. Symbols used must be listed in a transcriber’s note or placed on the Special Symbols page.

blocks.features: Three numbered items ('1.', '2.', '3.'), all-caps title text; item 2 alone carries a print bullet (a small solid round dot) before its number to flag it for special attention; items 1 and 3 have no bullet.

items.text: THE LIFE AND TIMES OF SHERLOCK HOLMES

print.surroundingText: Immediately follows rule 8.7.1.b; Example 8-5b on the same page shows the identical list with a different bullet symbol.
print.printFeatures: Boxed list; numbered items 1-3, all-caps; item 2's bullet is a small solid round (filled) dot to its left.

braille.notes: Bullet symbol '_4' (the one-cell 'Dot' transcriber-defined bullet listed under 8.6.2.a) precedes item 2's number, occupying cell 1 followed by a space before '#b4'; items 1 and 3 have no bullet and begin directly with the number sign in cell 1, per 8.7.1.a-b. Shown lines are 5-9 of the braille page (line 5 and line 9 blank, lines 6-8 the three items).

resolution: braille.lines byte-identical between A and B. Print casing: confirmed ALL-CAPS directly against the PDF page image (p. 204) — A was right ("THE LIFE AND TIMES OF SHERLOCK HOLMES" etc.), B’s Title-Case retyping was wrong; A’s text kept. illustrates.quote: A’s was missing clause a’s final sentence ("Symbols used must be listed…") — restored from the source (lines 251-254); B had merged in clause b’s text too, which this example does not itself illustrate (no runover is shown), so rule stays "8.7.1.a" alone. Item 2 carries BOTH its ordinal marker ("2.") and a print bullet (round dot, "•", confirmed against the page image) — recorded as a separate `bullet:"dot"` field since Emboss’s list formatter has no way to combine an ordinal marker with a bullet indicator (F-33 extension); buildModel8 records this as a limitation rather than guessing a combined rendering.
